marks.gloss_en: טעמא דראשו מת, הא ראשו חי -- הבא אחריו בכור לנחלה נמי לא הוי
the reason [the next is a firstborn for inheritance] is that its head emerged dead; had its head emerged alive, the one after it would not be a firstborn for inheritance either
מאי טעמא? יכיר אמר רחמנא (kind svara: a verse given as reason, no תא שמע)
Reish Lakish: the forehead [emerging] exempts everywhere
מאי קראה? הכרת פניהם ענתה בם (kind svara: a verse for the baraita's rule, no תא שמע)
תא שמע: פדחת בלא פרצוף פנים ... עד שיהו שניהם עם החוטם -- the forehead alone does not identify
שאני עדות אשה דאחמירו בה רבנן (= p_achmiru_edut_isha, itself challenged at 46b.13)
the baraita: forehead without countenance, countenance without forehead -- one does not testify until both are [seen] with the nose
תנן: הבא אחר נפלים שיצא ראשו חי ... קתני מיהא ראשו! -- the mishna has the nefel's HEAD exempt the next, against Shmuel
מאי ראשו? רובו (= p_rosho_rubo; undone by 46b.4-8, which ends in the teyuvta)
the stam's answer: what is 'its head' [in the mishna's nefel clause]? most of it
מיתיבי: יכיר -- הכרת פנים, פרצוף פנים עם החוטם -- recognition needs more than the forehead
תני: עד החוטם -- read the baraita as 'up to the nose'
תא שמע: אין מעידים אלא על פרצוף פנים עם החוטם
תני: עד החוטם
the baraita: 'he shall recognize' -- this is recognition of the face; and what is recognition of the face? the countenance with the nose
ואיבעית אימא: יכיר לחוד והכרת פנים לחוד (47a.1; = p_yakir_lechud)
ומי אחמירו? והא תנן: הוחזקו להיות משיאים עד מפי עד, מפי אשה, מפי עבד, מפי שפחה!
כי אקילו רבנן בסופה, בתחלתה לא אקילו -- lenient about who reports, not about the identification itself
the mishna: they established [the practice] of permitting [a woman] to marry on the testimony of a witness from a witness, a woman, a slave, a maidservant
Shmuel: [emergence of] the head does not exempt in the case of nefalim
the reason: 'all in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life' (Gen 7:22)
the Chullin mishna: [a fetus that] put out its head, even though it withdrew it, is as born
[a human] cannot be learned from an animal, for it has no prozdor
an animal cannot be learned from a human, because a human's countenance is significant
the Nidda mishna: [a child] emerging in the usual way [is born] once most of its head has emerged; and what is most of its head? once its forehead emerges
'everywhere' comes to include the baraita's case of the convert
